name: Revisionist Zionism
summary: Revisionist Zionism, founded by Ze'ev Jabotinsky in the 1920s, demanded an openly stated Jewish state with a Jewish majority on both banks of the Jordan, to be secured by military strength behind an iron wall of force. It rejected socialism and class struggle in favour of national unity, private enterprise and compulsory arbitration, and was institutionally embodied in Betar, the Irgun, Herut and later Likud. Its mainstream favoured liberal parliamentary government and civil rights for Arabs as a minority, while an Irgun wing was harder-line.
scope: Jabotinsky's Revisionist movement (Hatzohar, the New Zionist Organization, Betar) and its Herut and Likud heirs under Begin, based on the Iron Wall essay, the Encyclopaedia Judaica entry and the 1977 Likud platform. Excludes Lehi's fascist-leaning wing and later religious-settler Zionism. Economic and social questions the movement did not address are answered as neutral or low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Herut later backed national health insurance, but the Revisionist founding program was built around private initiative, so adherents are split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Later Herut supported a minimum wage while the Jabotinsky-era program stressed private capital and national over class interests; no settled line.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Revisionists favoured private initiative and private capital with minimal state involvement, against Labor's Histadrut economy.

public-ownership.rationale: Revisionism opposed the Labor movement's collectively owned economic sector and favoured private enterprise in industry.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not a programmatic issue; inferred from the bourgeois, pro-private-capital orientation.

unions-good.rationale: Revisionists rejected class struggle, built a rival labor body to the Histadrut and sought compulsory arbitration with strikes banned during state-building.

property-fundamental.rationale: Jabotinsky held private property necessary for liberty, though national goals could override it in practice.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from the preference for minimal state involvement in industry; the sources do not address corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Herut later accepted social legislation while the early program was pro-capital; adherents are split and the sources are thin.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership was the Labor Zionist model that Revisionists opposed in favour of private enterprise and class cooperation.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security-first orientation (Likud pledge to eliminate terror organizations) implies acceptance, but surveillance is not discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the national-discipline and traditionalist ethos of Betar-style education.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the liberal-parliamentary strand and the nationalist strand would pull in different directions.

strong-leader.rationale: Jabotinsky's centralised, leader-led movement drew comparison with European right-wing movements, and he doubted democracy outside England.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement's whole purpose was to build a Jewish state, which Jabotinsky said was the main thing.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; Betar valued Jewish armed self-defense but civilian gun policy is not a Revisionist question.

empower-police-military.rationale: Military strength was central: the iron wall doctrine and the Jewish Legion and army demands.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's conservative national-education emphasis.

decide-locally.rationale: The program centred on a unified, sovereign state over the whole land; localism is not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Not a central theme; inferred from the nationalist cultural conservatism and pride in Jewish tradition.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not an issue in the founding era; Likud-aligned adherents have mostly been conservative or split, inferred only.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between secular liberals and traditionalists.

more-religion-public.rationale: Revisionism was neutral on religious questions, with Jabotinsky saying only that a state mattered, not whether it was Orthodox.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; no position in the sources.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the nationalist-traditional cultural stance.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The New Zionist Organization aimed at reviving the Jewish state and language, and Betar taught glorification of the nation and its way of life.

gradual-change.rationale: Revisionism was a revision of gradual practical Zionism, demanding an explicit state goal and mass immigration at once.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Revisionism sought mass Jewish immigration, with a 1.5 million evacuation plan, though this concerns Jewish immigration to the homeland; general policy is inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Jabotinsky relied on force and British power rather than international consent, and Likud rejected outside-imposed solutions and UN Resolution 242.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; private-capital preference does not settle the trade question.

nation-first.rationale: The movement put national interests above class and foreign pressure, with Likud pledging no handover of Judea and Samaria.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents emphasise force for national security rather than human-rights wars.

open-borders.rationale: Its program was a Jewish-majority state with secure borders held behind an iron wall.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the promise that private capital would end poverty.

revolution-justified.rationale: Revisionists backed armed struggle against the British, including the Irgun, but Jabotinsky favoured a legal parliamentary approach, so adherents split.

central-planning.rationale: Revisionists rejected the socialist planning of the Labor movement and favoured private capital.

socialized-markets.rationale: The worker- or public-owned model was Labor Zionism's, which Revisionists opposed.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from private-initiative orientation.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from the demand for minimal state involvement in industry.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Revisionists favoured private ownership generally, but a particular preference for small owners is not documented.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Revisionism rejected communism and class struggle and championed bourgeois private capital.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a conventional pro-capital stance.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Revisionists backed compulsory arbitration of labor disputes and a ban on strikes during state-building, close to state-set bargaining.

one-party-rule.rationale: Jabotinsky ruled out a police state and Herut was accepted as a parliamentary democratic party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not an issue; Jabotinsky imagined a state loyal to the British Empire but favoured parliamentary government.

democracy-best.rationale: The mainstream strand favoured British-style liberal democracy and parliamentary methods, despite Jabotinsky's doubts about democracy abroad.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power belongs to the socialist tradition Revisionists opposed.

right-to-secede.rationale: Likud insisted on exclusive Israeli sovereignty between the sea and the Jordan and refused to give up territory.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's leader cult is documented but no doctrine of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Irgun carried out armed attacks, and Jabotinsky argued enforced justice is still justice.

war-builds-character.rationale: Betar taught martial discipline and that Jews survive by fighting back, but this is not an explicit doctrine about war's value.

separate-church-state.rationale: Revisionism was neutral on religion; it did not push either strict separation or a religious state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Jabotinsky stressed that the state need not be Orthodox, and Revisionism did not rest its claims on religious doctrine.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement demanded a strong state army and rejected non-state defense of the Jewish national home.

military-superiority.rationale: The iron wall holds that only a force the Arabs cannot overcome secures the Jewish state.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The goal was a state with a Jewish majority, though Arabs would hold full civil rights.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Revisionists explicitly rejected class struggle and put national interests first.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The movement rejected socialist egalitarianism while promising a bourgeois regime would end poverty.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Jabotinsky argued that native populations resist colonists but self-determination should not protect existing possession against landless peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Iron Wall's defence of colonization.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; Revisionism pursued a specifically Jewish national state.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Betar education put the national idea above individual status.

limit-population.rationale: Revisionism sought a large Jewish population and mass immigration, so limiting growth runs against it.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the pro-development urban and capital emphasis.

restore-past-order.rationale: The program aimed at building a new state rather than restoring an old order, though it did cite historic right.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Revisionists took pride in lacking a clear ideology beyond the state goal, inferred as pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: The Irgun used direct armed action while the mainstream pursued parliamentary and diplomatic routes.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contrary to a modernising, urban-development program.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A communist aim that Revisionism rejected.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Revisionists opposed communist distribution and favoured private enterprise.

production-for-use.rationale: Their economics rested on private capital and profit-seeking enterprise.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Revisionists rejected class struggle and Marxist analysis and defended private capital.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Jabotinsky opposed communism and a communist police state.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective kibbutz-type farming was the Labor Zionist model, which Revisionists opposed.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist thesis rejected by a movement favouring private capital. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not a stated position; Revisionists wanted a strong state, though minimal in industry.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Jabotinsky saw Arabs as a national minority with minority rights, so group status mattered, and the nation took priority over individual status.

conscription.rationale: Betar and the Revisionist program stressed a Jewish army and defense education; inferred as support for conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to a state for the Jewish people and to mass emigration to it.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; the state is treated as a national instrument, not a firm.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed in founding sources; later Likud rhetoric is outside the scope.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not a Revisionist doctrine; Jabotinsky's nationalism was civic-cultural, inferred only.

organic-representation.rationale: Not part of the program, which favoured parliamentary democracy.

total-state.rationale: Jabotinsky explicitly ruled out a police state of the fascist or communist sort.

national-rebirth.rationale: Revisionism sought a national revival of the Jewish people, state and language.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The aim was a Jewish state on both banks of the Jordan and later all of western Eretz Israel, though framed as historic right rather than imperial expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A feudal model with no place in a modern parliamentary national movement. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

bound-labor.rationale: Alien to the program. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a conventional national-liberal outlook.

universal-morality.rationale: Jabotinsky argued that Zionism is moral and just and that justice enforced is still justice, appealing to a universal standard.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The founding demand: a Jewish-majority state, with Likud calling the right to Eretz Israel eternal and indisputable.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Revisionists planned mass immigration and evacuation of European Jews, and Likud called on diaspora Jews to settle the land.

revive-national-language.rationale: The New Zionist Organization aimed at the revival of the Jewish state and Hebrew language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Rejected by a movement that stressed class cooperation and private enterprise.

economic-freedom.rationale: Jabotinsky saw private property as necessary for liberty and promoted private initiative.

rule-by-example.rationale: The program relied on law, military force and parliamentary institutions, not rulers' example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement's basic principle was Jewish national self-determination in a state, with Jabotinsky saying self-determination means revision.

force-without-un.rationale: Jabotinsky and later Likud relied on force and rejected externally imposed solutions, including UN Resolution 242.

class-collaboration.rationale: Revisionists emphasised national over class interests, rejected class struggle and backed compulsory arbitration.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement stressed Jewish tradition and national culture.

dominated-front.rationale: Jabotinsky sought alliance with the British Empire, not a front against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Revisionists put the national idea ahead of class and rejected international socialism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; Revisionist sources assume civil equality.

ban-interest.rationale: A bourgeois, private-capital program would not ban lending. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Jabotinsky envisioned Arabs with full civil and minority rights, not racial segregation law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist thesis rejected by a movement denying class struggle. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; Jewish immigrants were to join a national culture but the sources do not state a line.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not a Revisionist doctrine, inferred only.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Israeli system was proportional and Revisionist successors operated in it; no stated doctrine though.

national-mission.rationale: Zionism aimed at a Jewish national home rather than exporting a government form.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a non-feminist national program.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Herut campaigned as an opposition against the Labor establishment, but the sources do not frame this as corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not a Revisionist doctrine and contrary to its liberal strand; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Begin resigned after Sabra and Shatila criticism but the movement defended its forces, inferred only.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Revisionists wanted minimal state in industry but a strong state for defense and state-building, and later accepted some social legislation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Jabotinsky favoured equal civil rights for Arabs in principle, though the Irgun wing opposed power-sharing.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist debate foreign to Revisionism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Jabotinsky described Zionism as colonization yet insisted it is moral and just, so adherents reject the pejorative framing.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; Jabotinsky's liberal strand implies equal law while religious parties demanded personal-status law.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Revisionism was neutral on religious questions.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist doctrine not applicable, though the security logic of strength against hostile neighbours is shared.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The liberal strand favoured parliamentary democracy, though Jabotinsky argued Arab consent to Zionism would never be voluntary.

population-transfer.rationale: Jabotinsky's statements on transfer were inconsistent, sometimes supportive and sometimes envisioning Arabs in a democracy, and he denied wanting expulsion; Likud pledged not to dispossess anyone.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Betar taught that Jews might strike first, and the Iron Wall defends enforced justice.

separated-powers.rationale: The parliamentary, legalist strand accepted liberal constitutional forms; not explicitly stated.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine opposed by Revisionists. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Jabotinsky promised a regime would eliminate poverty but not through priority-to-poor legislation.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Likud's later policy, in line with private property, but not a founding position.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Revisionists banned strikes and lockouts during state-building and favoured compulsory arbitration.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Revisionism attributed poverty to the lack of a bourgeois regime rather than population.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contrary to parliamentary elections favoured by the movement. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Security-minded, though the liberal strand resists; inferred and uncertain.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from the preference for free private enterprise.

party-controls-media.rationale: Jabotinsky rejected a police state and Herut accepted parliamentary democracy.

party-commands-army.rationale: Revisionists built armed forces for the nation and not as party formations in a state, though Irgun was a party-aligned militia before statehood.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Jewish immigrants were to gain immediate citizenship, but others' rules are not stated.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A radical-egalitarian idea alien to the bourgeois program. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Betar and Hatzohar were disciplined, leader-led organisations; no explicit doctrine.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The movement insisted on sovereignty and rejected externally imposed arrangements.

clerical-rule.rationale: Revisionism was neutral on religion and did not rest its claims on religious authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revisionists supported fighting alongside the Allies and cooperated with national armies, and rejected defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the liberal civil-liberty aims.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Jabotinsky sought British alliance and the Jewish state loyal to the Empire.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Contrary to the private-property, private-capital program. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

people-in-arms.rationale: Betar and Irgun urged armed Jewish self-defense but the movement also demanded a regular Jewish army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: After the 1926-27 crises Revisionists shifted toward urban development and private capital against the Labor agrarian ideal.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Revisionists claimed both banks of the Jordan and rejected partition, which resembles reunification of a divided land; the statement is not specifically addressed.

death-penalty.rationale: Likud pledged to eliminate terror organizations and later Likud figures backed executing terrorists; no founding doctrine.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was largely secular and neutral on religion.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Jewish return is by descent for the diaspora but the general rule for citizenship is not stated.

minority-language-support.rationale: Jabotinsky favoured minority legal rights, but language funding is not stated.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; Betar education stressed conformity to national discipline.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Revisionists treated statehood as the aim and economic transformation as secondary to national independence.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Banning strikes during state-building suggests some willingness but political freedoms are otherwise defended.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from the military-self-reliance doctrine of the iron wall.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Likud's platform says Judea and Samaria will not be handed to foreign administration and that only Israeli sovereignty will hold between the sea and the Jordan.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The movement favoured private enterprise but never addressed central banking; adherents have no settled line.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Revisionists rejected class-based socialism and favoured private initiative, though with national duties; inferred that owners are not held in trust for the community.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Revisionists opposed socialism and regarded the USSR as a socialist or communist state; the state-capitalist label is inferred to be foreign to them.

precautionary-principle.rationale: A 1920s-30s nationalist movement never addressed environmental risk; no basis for a line.

collective-defense.rationale: The movement stressed Jewish self-defence behind an iron wall of its own force, yet Jabotinsky also sought alliances with Britain and Poland, so adherents are split.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Likud's platform asserts Israeli sovereignty over Judea and Samaria and rejects the view that held land is occupied or should be given to foreign administration.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Revisionist platform stressed respect for religion and the Jewish tradition while remaining liberal, so state curbing of religious property is not part of it; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A liberal parliamentary model with a ceremonial president is the mainstream Revisionist view; no source states it directly.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The movement's emphasis on force, territorial integrity and a single Jewish-majority state implies readiness to keep a territory by force; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Adherents favoured minority rights and later Likud autonomy plans for Arabs, but no settled position on regions keeping their own legal and economic systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Jabotinsky's liberal-parliamentary, secular-nationalist movement had no divine-ruler idea; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The movement defended private enterprise and rejected class politics, which suggests lighter, less redistributive taxes; no tax rule is stated, so inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: The movement did not take a settled line on nature versus nurture; its stress on educating a new Jew in Betar sits against talk of national character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Mainstream Revisionists favoured liberal parliamentary government and civil rights under law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed by a movement of the 1920s-70s, and no inference follows from its principles.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The movement favoured parliamentary democracy; no stated view on a few-and-many blend.

leader-cult.rationale: Betar honoured Jabotinsky as its leader, but mainstream Revisionism was liberal and parliamentary and did not adopt state leader worship; inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Revisionism rejected socialism and class struggle in favour of national unity and compulsory arbitration.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from its stress on private enterprise and property; no land-redistribution plank is documented.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred: a Jewish majority was the movement's aim, which a mass return of Arab refugees would undermine.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Its territorial claim rested on historic right and Jewish national need, not on co-nationals living there; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from its liberal parliamentary outlook and civil rights; religious penalties are not part of the program.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from its secular-liberal civil-rights outlook; no such demand appears in the program.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from nationalist insistence on sovereignty and self-reliance; the issue is anachronistic.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Its aim was one Jewish state in Palestine, not union of kindred peoples across borders; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Jabotinsky-era programs offered minorities cultural and national rights inside the Jewish state; inferred from its minority-rights platform.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: It held that diaspora Jews should emigrate and its platform called for evacuating the diaspora to a Jewish state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: It replaced Marxist class analysis with a national-spirit view of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: The program stressed private capital but also state arbitration; no settled line on antitrust.

no-bailouts.rationale: No documented position; adherents split between free-enterprise and state-led traditions.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Its mainstream favoured liberal parliamentary government with civil rights, implying limits on majorities; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred: quotas are not in the program and its private-initiative outlook favours merit and voters.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from reliance on private enterprise and overseas Jewish capital rather than a closed bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents have no distinctive line on trade conditions.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: it emphasised national duty but built its economics on private enterprise and incentive.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Its Irgun wing launched an armed revolt against British rule, though the mainstream was divided; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from its liberal outlook; no support for hereditary rank is documented.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on Hebrew national culture and revival; curricula are not discussed in the sources.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Iron Wall rejects the pretence that colonisation benefits the Arab population, grounding the claim in national self-interest instead.

patriotic-education.rationale: Betar and the movement stressed national pride, discipline and symbols; inferred for schools.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Revisionists stressed equal rights for citizens but no position on preferences is documented.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from private enterprise and opposition to socialism; central-bank questions are not addressed.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Revisionists favoured private enterprise and rejected class-struggle collapse theory; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a movement that sought its own state rather than influence over others.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from support for private enterprise and rejection of socialism.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The movement rejected class-struggle analysis and socialist theory.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Revisionism stressed civil rights and equality before the law and property rights, so open discrimination is inferred as disfavoured.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Likud platform and Jabotinsky's constitutional draft favour guaranteed civil rights; entrenchment is inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Revisionists contested the British Mandate's terms and demanded both banks of the Jordan; the general rule about colonial treaties is not stated.

elective-rulers.rationale: Revisionism called for a liberal parliamentary government with elected rulers and civil rights; elective government is inferred as standard.

minority-veto.rationale: Revisionism put national unity and a majority-based state first; an individual veto is inferred to be rejected.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Jabotinsky's liberalism and rule of law lead to the view that rulers bound by law may be resisted; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Revisionists favoured a liberal parliamentary government, and parliament is inferred as the supreme lawmaker.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed in the movement's texts; liberal humanism of Jabotinsky is the basis, so a mild yes is inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; animal use is assumed, with humane limits as part of general liberalism; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The movement stressed national unity and private enterprise without a stated duty of the rich; adherents are split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Revisionism demanded active nation-building, military training and political action, so withdrawal contradicts it.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The movement rejected the Marxist critique and held that national and military mobilisation of culture was legitimate; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Revisionists rejected class-analysis frameworks and class struggle in favour of national unity; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Revisionism favoured private enterprise and capital, not a dependency analysis; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Revisionism backed full civil rights and proportional representation for Arabs as a minority, so offices are not reserved by birth.

party-own-road.rationale: Not a communist movement; the statement is not applicable, so nothing settles it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Revisionism relied on Jewish self-defence and private capital, with distrust of external guarantees; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revisionism held that the whole of the Land of Israel on both banks of the Jordan belongs to the Jewish people, and Likud held that no territory will be given up.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Revisionism sought a Jewish majority state with minority rights for Arabs, not leadership by pre-existing inhabitants.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Jabotinsky opposed fascism, but anti-fascism as a constitutional founding value is not addressed.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Revisionists were hostile to both communism and Nazism, but were accused of fascist leanings; the equivalence claim is inferred and split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; the liberal mainstream reading holds that slavery was the cause, so inferred negative.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed in the movement's texts; nothing settles the question.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed in the movement's texts; nothing settles the question.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in the movement's texts; nothing settles the question.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Revisionists framed Zionism as a Western-liberal European enterprise, so cultural relativism about institutions is inferred to be rejected.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Revisionism stressed military strength, the Irgun and the army as the force securing the state, but it also backed civilian rule; inferred from the iron wall.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed in the movement's texts; nothing settles the question.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditionalist, national-unity outlook; it set no doctrine on family duty.

office-by-exam.rationale: The movement never addressed civil-service selection; adherents' views are not documented.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the Likud emphasis on national strength and security, though the platform also backs private enterprise.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; religious-secular splits in Herut and Likud leave adherents divided.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Revisionism favoured liberal parliamentary government and national unity over mandated delegates; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Revisionists backed private enterprise, but Herut and Likud later supported national insurance, so adherents are split.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Revisionism rejected socialist land programmes in favour of private enterprise; inferred, though it backed national land purchase.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Revisionists endorsed liberal parliamentary government, which implies parliamentary control of spending.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the movement's insistence on Hebrew as the national language of a Jewish state.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stressed Jewish land purchase and settlement but set no doctrine on foreign ownership.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from its individualist, liberal-civil-rights outlook and focus on national rather than racial-group equality.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed; national unity and private enterprise do not settle the question.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the movement's belief in force and the Irgun's own armed struggle; the Iron Wall is about local settlement.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Never addressed; the doctrine concerns force against a local population, not alliance management.

corporate-influence.rationale: The programme backed private enterprise and national over class interest; corporate influence is inferred as not a concern.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the movement's nationalism and security focus; the sources do not address foreign NGO funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the demand for a Jewish majority, which makes demographic growth a national aim.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; Likud's settlement policy favoured Jewish settlement but no residents-only rule is stated.

job-guarantee.rationale: The programme favoured private initiative and compulsory arbitration, not state-guaranteed jobs.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; the Iron Wall rests on force rather than regime type.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Betar discipline and respect for law coexisted with Irgun rebellion against Mandate law; adherents are split.

non-intervention.rationale: The Iron Wall rests on settlement backed by force and Revisionists championed Jewish rights abroad; non-intervention is inferred as disfavoured.

industrial-unions.rationale: Revisionists opposed the class-based Histadrut and favoured national organisation and arbitration; industry unions are inferred as disfavoured.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream's liberal, civil-rights stance; the sources do not address conspiracy claims directly.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the movement's national and traditional outlook; not addressed in the sources.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The mainstream favoured liberal parliamentary government, from which access to government information is inferred.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed by the programme; adherents have no stated view.

informal-organisation.rationale: Betar and the Irgun were disciplined hierarchical organisations built around a national movement and later parties.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on national sovereignty; the sources do not address international courts.

religious-nation.rationale: Jabotinsky defined the Jewish nation by national rather than religious criteria, and the Revisionists were largely secular; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the demand for a self-reliant state secured by its own force, not by patronage of a protector.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no clear position found in its platform.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The movement rejected socialism and class struggle in favour of private enterprise, so common ownership of productive means is opposed.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of socialism and hostility to the left, though no stated campaign against communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from the support for private enterprise combined with compulsory arbitration and a state role.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred: Jabotinsky was secular but the movement respected tradition, and no doctrine of religion as illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of private enterprise as the basis of national growth.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the movement's national-unity focus; it did not frame women's equality in economic terms.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the collectivist kibbutz model of communal childcare.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Hebrew revival was shared across Zionism; no stated policy to purge loanwords.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed directly; minority rights were promised but within a Jewish-majority state.

cooperative-communities.rationale: It rejected the socialist communal settlement model (kibbutz) in favour of private enterprise and national unity.

majority-settlement.rationale: It demanded mass Jewish colonisation to create a majority, and Likud's platform pledges settlement across the land.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: it was a nationalist, pro-private-enterprise doctrine but did not reject capitalism itself.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Revisionism founded its demand for a Jewish state on both banks of the Jordan on the Jewish historical bond to the land, ahead of the claims of its Arab residents.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred because the movement's own history and its Holocaust-era rescue campaigns make denial unthinkable to adherents.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream's liberal parliamentary outlook and civil-rights commitments; the sources do not address the issue.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The mainstream favoured liberal parliamentary government and civil rights, including for the Arab minority, rather than suppressing opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from the movement's secular national character; it never sought state punishment of religious dissent.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from its own colonising-settler nationalism, which sought a home for a people rather than rule over distant subjects for the metropole's profit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the movement is a Jewish nationalism with no stake in Islamic duty, and it treated Arab resistance as a political, not religious, fact to be met with force.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from its secular, liberal-parliamentary outlook, which gives no role to removing rulers for lacking religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from its preference for national unity and representative parliamentary government over direct, grassroots decision-making.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of class struggle in favour of national unity; it treated the national question as the one to address first.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The movement never addressed gender identity, and adherents today are split between liberal and conservative views.

assisted-dying.rationale: The sources are silent on assisted dying and adherents are split between liberal and religious-conservative positions.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred from its identification as a distinct national-liberal right wing of Zionism that opposed the socialist left.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of socialism and class analysis, which it replaced with national unity and private enterprise.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from Jabotinsky's view that Arabs and Jews could be reconciled only by strength; adherents did not frame Islam as incompatible with the West.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred from the movement's secular nationalism, which grounds authority in the nation and its parliament rather than in God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and adherents are split between secular and traditionalist views.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the movement's private-enterprise stance gives no clear answer on workplace harassment rules.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred from its support for private enterprise combined with compulsory arbitration and national unity, which sit between laissez-faire and state control.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The iron wall doctrine rests on military strength as the guarantee of the Jewish state, so abolishing armed forces is the opposite of its programme.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from its support for private enterprise and its rejection of equalising class politics, which allows unequal starts.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: the movement sought allies among the great powers, notably Britain, and Likud later aligned with the West, rather than neutrality.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream Revisionist commitment to liberal parliamentary government; hereditary office was never part of the platform.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of private enterprise and capital; user-owned mutual credit was a cooperative-socialist idea it did not take up.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The movement never addressed international lenders; a Likud-style stress on national self-reliance is offset by its market orientation, so adherents split.

property-franchise.rationale: Revisionists backed liberal parliamentary government with civil rights for all citizens, which implies a broad franchise rather than a wealth test.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: the movement had no ecological or feminist theory of domination, and its liberal-national outlook treats these as separate questions.

reification.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of Marxism and class analysis; it saw markets as compatible with national unity rather than as a veil over social relations.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from its defence of private enterprise and liberal civil rights; the movement treated press and assembly freedoms as real.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from its liberal parliamentary mainstream, which favoured constitutional rule; the Irgun wing was harder-line and the sources do not discuss decrees directly.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Revisionist programme and the Likud platform promised equal civil rights to Arab citizens within a Jewish-majority state, so race-based voting was rejected.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: the movement predates the internet and had no position, and nothing in its principles settles the question.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from its liberal parliamentary outlook; the sources do not address publication of government records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The sources do not address marriage law; adherents ranged from secular Revisionists to religious supporters, so no settled line.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: Revisionism sought a Jewish state with civil rights for Arabs and the Likud platform pledged no dispossession, so a boycott of minority shops was not its programme.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Revisionism favoured parliamentary government and national unity under elected leadership; inferred from that, as sortition assemblies were never discussed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Revisionism was secular-national and left religious law to the religious; inferred from its non-religious character, as the question was not addressed.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the Revisionist rejection of class struggle and its defence of private enterprise and national unity; low confidence.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents of Jabotinsky's liberal individualism and the religious-traditional wing would split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: a national movement built on Jewish peoplehood and liberal parliamentary government would not impose atheism through schools.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from the Iron Wall's reliance on force and armed security as the basis of the state.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Jabotinsky proposed minority civil rights but a Jewish-majority state; executive power-sharing is not clearly stated, so adherents split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from Revisionist support for private enterprise and national solidarity; low confidence.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the movement or the 1977 Likud platform.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the Revisionist preference for liberal parliamentary government; direct delegation is not discussed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from secular liberals to religious traditionalists.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from Revisionist liberal parliamentary principles, which included equal civil rights; low confidence.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Revisionism sought a Jewish-majority state with civil rights for minorities but tied the franchise to citizenship; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: The movement favoured private enterprise and rejected socialism, so state price caps run against it; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; the pro-private-enterprise outlook points to defending property rights, inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Betar, the Revisionist youth movement, was a uniformed and drilled organisation training youth for national service and defence.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; Likud-era Israel holds nuclear capability and its heirs reject this limit; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Jabotinsky's Iron Wall initially relied on a foreign (British) force, and the later movement stressed Jewish self-reliance, so the issue is not settled.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not directly addressed; the movement stressed Jewish national memory and the persecution of Jews, so adherents would support formal recognition; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Revisionists rejected class struggle and favoured private enterprise and arbitration, but did not address this question directly.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Iron Wall argues that a settlement can only follow a force the other side cannot overcome, which rejects any absolute bar on killing.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Zionism rests on the claim of Jewish continuity to the ancient homeland, and the Likud platform affirms Jewish rights in the land; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; no source for this view, so inferred from the movement's conventional outlook.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's conventional outlook.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Revisionism honoured its fallen fighters, including executed Irgun members, as national heroes and martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Jabotinsky's movement was secular and liberal-nationalist, framing politics as a national and military contest; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Revisionism demanded a Jewish state with a Jewish majority and mass immigration, against the cultural-centre idea of the Zionist spiritual school.

culture-before-state.rationale: Revisionism was political Zionism that put statehood and military strength first, against cultural Zionism's priority on renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: The movement was secular-national and never addressed how God is described, and adherents are split between secular and religious members; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's conventional outlook suggests rejecting this; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The movement sought a Jewish-majority state but with equal civil rights for Arabs as a minority, so reserving the economy for the majority was not its program.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Revisionism sought a single Jewish state across both banks of the Jordan; read loosely as one territorial unit for one people; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: The Revisionists opposed the Histadrut and favoured compulsory arbitration of labour disputes, restricting strikes.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The movement rejected socialism and class struggle for national unity, so socialist tests are not its concern.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Private enterprise was favoured but no position on local services is recorded; adherents are split.

second-chamber.rationale: The platform stressed parliamentary government but the sources do not say whether a second chamber was favoured.

municipal-property.rationale: Revisionism backed private enterprise and national unity; communal ownership is contrary to its platform.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The movement was nationalist and centralised around a state; confederal local assemblies are inferred against.

family-wage.rationale: The program was built on private initiative and says nothing on family wages.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Its state-building nationalism is inferred to favour state financial control; not discussed.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic to the movement; no basis for a position.

person-over-state.rationale: Mainstream Revisionism embraced liberal parliamentary government and civil rights, with Jabotinsky stressing the individual.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Jabotinsky was secular but respected religious tradition in the platform; adherents are split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The platform does not address regional government within a state.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from pro-development, private-enterprise settlement; not discussed.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Revisionism organised on national, not racial, lines and asked for Arab minority civil rights; inferred against racial organising.

racial-pride.rationale: National pride was central to Betar's culture; extended to pride in ancestry by inference.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Iron Wall holds force necessary to secure a Jewish state on both banks of the Jordan, which goes beyond pure self-defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Revisionists defined the Jewish nation by shared history and descent across many languages and states; inferred, though Hebrew was promoted.

communal-electorates.rationale: Jabotinsky promised Arabs full civil rights in a liberal parliamentary state with proportional shares (s3), implying common rather than communal electorates; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Revisionists were suspicious of British policy but the movement did not centre a partition plot; inferred as split.

free-public-college.rationale: The platform stressed private enterprise and national arbitration (s3), not free public services; inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; inferred as neutral.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on national continuity and building the homeland for later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The movement did not address gendered values; inferred as neutral.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Iron Wall essay makes military strength the basis of security and of any eventual agreement with the Arabs (s1), so arms reduction runs against it.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on force and national interest over open multilateral diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: The platform favoured private enterprise and rejected class-based statism (s3); inferred that capital should move freely.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the Revisionist insistence on a state with a proper military; the Irgun was disbanded into the army in 1948.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Iron Wall rests on military strength and unflinching force, so refusing orders to fight is contrary to its core.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Revisionists rejected class struggle and favoured compulsory arbitration, so unions bargaining freely was not their model.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The movement stressed private enterprise but the sources name no position on tax credits for low-paid families.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Revisionists favoured private enterprise but the sources say nothing about binding borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The movement did not address the world economic order; neutral by default.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The mainstream favoured liberal parliamentary government and legal means, not overthrowing the state machinery.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Revisionists opposed socialist class-based collective experiments such as the Labour Zionist settlements, preferring private enterprise and national unity.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Environmental accounting is outside the movement's concerns; nothing in the sources bears on it.

sacred-nation.rationale: The movement put the nation and national unity above class, though in a liberal rather than mystical register.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of state-led social programmes in favour of private enterprise.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from its stress on national unity and a single Jewish majority state; regional-exploitation framing is not part of it.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream's liberal civil-rights outlook, which assumes universal rights.

public-service-media.rationale: The sources name no position on public broadcasting; the 1977 Likud platform does not address it.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Revisionism was largely secular-national and took no stand on the unity of religions; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: The founding program stressed private initiative, so guaranteed crop prices would be unlikely; inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the Likud 1977 platform's emphasis on security and deterrence; nuclear weapons are not mentioned.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Revisionist platform opposed class struggle and favoured compulsory arbitration, putting the nation above class, so a separate workers' party was rejected.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the movement's liberal commitment to individual equal rights; FGM is not discussed.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Revisionist platform backed equal civil rights, including for women, so equal property rights fit; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The platform treated Hebrew as the national language but never addressed naming across regions; inferred neutral.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Private initiative and liberal property rights suggest openness to liability, but the movement never addressed pollution; adherents split.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the secular national program, which gave no official lawmaking role to traditional authorities.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the liberal, development-minded outlook; environment was not an issue for the movement.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The movement stressed security and law, but sentencing policy was not addressed; adherents split.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the platform's emphasis on Hebrew as the national language of the Jewish homeland.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of class struggle and the Histadrut's labour monopoly in favour of national unity and arbitration; adherents rarely addressed compulsory dues directly.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a liberal-parliamentary outlook that gives no clear lean on ID rules.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the movement's liberal, civil-rights framing and secular leadership, which kept religion out of the state's legal hierarchy.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The mainstream favoured liberal parliamentary government, so free competitive elections were the core test; inferred, not a stated doctrine.

premarital-sex.rationale: The movement did not address sexual morality; adherents ranged from secular to traditional.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the mainstream's liberal civil-rights commitments, though security-minded adherents would allow exceptions.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; private enterprise was favoured but adherents later backed welfare measures, so they are split.

women-suffrage.rationale: Revisionism's liberal parliamentary mainstream took equal civil and political rights as given; inferred from the platform's liberalism rather than a specific text.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's secular-liberal character and its alliance with religious parties, which make this a minority view.

race-social-construct.rationale: Jabotinsky wrote in terms of nation and race, but later adherents are split; the issue was not a doctrinal one.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed; adherents who favoured small government and those who favoured state action would split.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the movement's support for private enterprise and rejection of socialism.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on military strength and sovereignty over reliance on outside bodies.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred; Jabotinsky's movement was nationalist and secular-liberal, resting its case on national right and not on scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream's liberal parliamentary government and civil rights for minorities.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The movement rejected socialism and class struggle, so defending a planned, nationalised economy is far from its position.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream's liberal parliamentary government, in which voters elect their representatives directly.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the movement's liberal parliamentary stance and the lack of any church-state programme in the sources.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred; the movement wanted a Jewish-majority state with rights for Arabs as a minority, not territorial autonomy for them.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The Iron Wall holds that the local population will not consent, and the Likud platform vests sovereignty in Israel alone, so a local vote is rejected.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from the demand for a Jewish state on both banks of the Jordan, which meant redrawing the Mandate's frontiers.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the movement's focus on national strength and private enterprise, not austerity or self-sufficiency.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the Likud platform's support for Jewish settlement throughout the land, which opposes limiting settlement by region.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; nothing indicates a stance on the question.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Revisionism rested on the claim that the Jewish people have a historic right to the land on both banks of the Jordan and must defend it, as the Iron Wall essay and Likud platform assert.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The movement favoured liberal parliamentary government and legal process; the question never arose, so this is inferred from that liberal-constitutional stance.

close-ties-china.rationale: China was not a factor in the movement's era; later Likud governments have pursued Chinese trade while relying on the United States, so no settled line.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Revisionism was a diaspora-centred movement that sought to protect Jewish communities abroad and press for their rights and evacuation, as the movement's programme and Betar activity show.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Its program stressed private enterprise and national over class interest, so it did not hold that resources belong equally to all; inferred from that economic stance.

self-ownership.rationale: Its liberal individualist strand and support for private initiative imply personal rights over body and labour, though the movement never framed it as self-ownership; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The movement left tax structure largely unaddressed beyond backing private enterprise, so adherents have no settled position.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Jabotinsky-era program stressed private capital and national unity while later Herut accepted welfare measures, so adherents are split.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Revisionism was organised through parties (Hatzohar, Herut) and accepted parliamentary politics, so it did not seek to bypass parties; inferred from its liberal-parliamentary mainstream.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Its commitment to private enterprise and equal civil rights implies opposition to special privileges for the connected, but the movement did not address it directly; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Revisionism was a secular national movement that dealt with religion only marginally, and adherents were split between secular and traditionalist outlooks.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Revisionism sought a modern state while honouring Jewish national tradition, but never framed this as a choice; adherents are not clearly in either camp.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The mainstream favoured liberal civil rights and equality before the law, so it would likely have allowed women this right; inferred, as the movement never addressed it.

national-resource-control.rationale: Its economic nationalism and aim of an independent Jewish state imply national control of resources; inferred, not stated in its sources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Revisionism favoured private enterprise and rejected socialist class struggle, which fits process-based fairness; the sources do not address distributive theory, so inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The movement's emphasis on private capital and enterprise suggests opposition to a new tax on finance; inferred, not discussed.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Revisionism did not address racial disadvantage in this sense; the question is anachronistic for the movement.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Revisionism stressed liberal parliamentary government and legality, though the Irgun wing defied British Mandate law; mainstream view inferred as procedural.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not addressed by the movement, which favoured private initiative and national development; no basis for a lean.

multipolar-world.rationale: Jabotinsky sought a great-power patron for the iron wall, and the question was not a Revisionist concern; inferred neutral.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Revisionism rejected Marxism and socialist class struggle in favour of private enterprise and national unity, so a labour theory of value is rejected.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Revisionism put nation above class and rejected socialism, but favoured national solidarity including compulsory arbitration between workers and employers; split on this framing.

material-over-identity.rationale: The question is framed for the left, which Revisionism opposed; it put national identity first, and the framing does not map onto it.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Revisionism rejected communism and socialism and favoured private enterprise under parliamentary government, so a communist-led market economy is opposed.

missingStatements.text: The Jewish people should have a state with a Jewish majority on both banks of the Jordan River.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1931 and later Revisionist demand was a Jewish-majority state on both sides of the Jordan, which no existing statement captures.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Revisionist territorial programme; covered loosely by territorial-expansion and jewish-state-israel and not a question other ideologies would take sides on.

missingStatements.text: A country should not give up land it claims as its historic homeland in exchange for peace agreements.
missingStatements.rationale: Likud's platform says Judea and Samaria will not be handed to foreign administration and that only Israeli sovereignty will hold between the sea and the Jordan.

missingStatements.text: Peaceful agreement with a local population opposed to settlement is impossible until that population despairs of stopping it by force.
missingStatements.rationale: The Iron Wall argues that no voluntary agreement is possible and that a force the natives cannot overcome must come first.
missingStatements.declined: A specific strategic argument (the Iron Wall) rather than a position other ideologies would take a side on; too narrow for the bank.

notes: The Irgun wing opposed power-sharing with Arabs, while centrist Revisionists favoured liberal democracy. Jabotinsky's statements on transfer were inconsistent. Economics were never fully worked out, so many economic answers are low confidence.
